title: Best Books for Bank Exams 2026: IBPS & SBI PO/Clerk
meta_description: Best books for bank exams 2026. One set works for IBPS and SBI PO/Clerk: RS Aggarwal quant & reasoning, SP Bakshi English, Arihant banking awareness. Subject-wise.

hero.one_liner: One solid book set covers IBPS PO, IBPS Clerk, SBI PO, and SBI Clerk. The syllabus overlaps heavily across all four.

intro: The good news for bank aspirants: IBPS PO, SBI PO, and clerk syllabi overlap heavily in Quant, Reasoning, and English. One book set serves all of them.
If you are just starting and unsure where to begin, three books cover about 70% of the common syllabus: RS Aggarwal for quant, RS Aggarwal for reasoning, and SP Bakshi for English.
Bank exams are speed games. Pick standard books, then drill sectional and full-length tests until accuracy under time becomes second nature.

buying_tips: Three books cover most of the common syllabus: RS Aggarwal quant, RS Aggarwal reasoning, and SP Bakshi English.
Buy print for concept books, use apps and free PDFs for daily practice and current affairs.
Keep banking awareness updated with RBI news, since printed books go stale on current data fast.

faqs.question: Can one book set work for both IBPS and SBI?
faqs.answer:
Yes. The Quant, Reasoning, and English syllabi overlap heavily across IBPS and SBI PO and Clerk.

One solid set serves all four exams; only the difficulty and descriptive paper differ.

faqs.question: Which books should a complete beginner start with?
faqs.answer:
RS Aggarwal for quant, RS Aggarwal for reasoning, and SP Bakshi for English cover about 70% of the syllabus.

Finish these with practice, then add banking awareness and mocks.

faqs.question: Do I need a separate book for SBI PO descriptive?
faqs.answer:
Yes. SBI PO Mains has a descriptive English paper that objective books do not cover.

Descriptive General English by Bakshi and Richa Sharma is built for exactly this.

faqs.question: How do I prepare banking awareness?
faqs.answer:
Use Arihant's Banking Awareness for the static base, then update with RBI press releases and financial news.

Printed books cannot keep up with current data, so pair them with monthly current affairs.

faqs.question: Is RS Aggarwal enough for bank quant?
faqs.answer:
For the foundation, yes. Add M Tyra's Quicker Maths for the speed and shortcuts bank exams demand.

Then move to timed sectional practice and mocks.

faqs.question: Are bank exam books different for PO and Clerk?
faqs.answer:
Mostly the same books work; PO is harder and adds descriptive writing and tougher DI.

Clerk needs the same base with more speed practice at a slightly easier level.

faqs.question: Should I buy books or use online material for bank prep?
faqs.answer:
Concept books are best in print for revision. Daily MCQ practice, mocks, and current affairs work well online.

A blend of both is what most successful candidates use.

faqs.question: How important are mock tests for bank exams?
faqs.answer:
Very. Bank exams are won on speed and accuracy under time, which only mocks build.

After finishing your books, mock tests should be your main daily activity.
